To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the telecommunications regulatory regime shifted from a stable, closed, and oligopolistic structure to an open one that encouraged competition; (ii) this shift provided opportunities to new entrants and entrepreneurs; and (iii) the regulatory shifts were driven in part by political dynamics of the time, and in part by the need for the government to address the telecommunications sector’s poor performance.

1) Japan’s telecommunications regulatory regime shifted from one that was dominated by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT) to a new regime dominated by the Ministry for Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and the Telecommunications Carriers Association (TCA), and 2) this shift created opportunities and protection for entrepreneurs in the telecommunications sector.
